subtype: Team hit by a late finisher [Receiver]
passage: At the NGO's Thursday review, Divyansh looked at the clock: 4:40. The grant report was due to the funder at nine the next morning, and it still lacked the beneficiary table that Saurabh had promised on Tuesday, then Wednesday. Divyansh had written every other section on time and now sat with a blank page and a folded-up plan. The table arrived at 6:15 in the evening with two columns missing. Divyansh phoned home to say dinner would be late again, ordered a cup of tea from the corner stall and began compressing three hours of checks into one. By 10 pm the report was finished, but tired hands had made three small mistakes that only showed the next day.

qa.q: At what time did the beneficiary table arrive?
qa.a: The table arrived at 6:15 in the evening with two columns missing.

qa.q: What was Divyansh feeling while phoning home to say dinner would be late?
qa.a: Divyansh was tired and frustrated, and worried about the deadline, since the late table meant staying on to compensate.

qa.q: What could Divyansh do next time when waiting for someone else's input?
qa.a: Ask Saurabh early for a firm date and a partial version, and warn the team when the date looks unsafe, so the report can be planned around it.

qa.q: How might Saurabh see the delay?
qa.a: Saurabh may not realise the cost to Divyansh, treating it as the table's own lateness, when in fact it fell on the person waiting.

grounding: A person waiting for someone else's late input compresses their own work and stays late to compensate.

subtype: Team hit by a late finisher [Receiver]
passage:
Subject: Friday's report and the late file

Dear Kamal,

I wanted to tell you plainly how Thursday looked from my side. Your figures came at 6:40 pm, and the client presentation was at nine the next morning. I had two hours of proofreading planned and ended up rebuilding the charts until 1 a.m. I'm not writing to blame you; I know the figures were tangled. But I was tired and a bit anxious on Friday, and I made a mistake on slide six. Could we agree that if a date looks shaky, you tell me the day before, and send whatever part you have? I can work with half a table. I can't work with none, late.

Thanks,
Asif

qa.q: At what time did Kamal's figures arrive on Thursday?
qa.a: Kamal's figures came at 6:40 pm.

qa.q: How does Asif feel about writing to Kamal?
qa.a: Asif feels careful and a little uneasy, wanting to explain without blaming, and states plainly that Friday was tiring and anxious.

qa.q: What does Asif ask Kamal to do in future?
qa.a: Asif asks Kamal to say the day before if a date looks shaky, and to send whatever part is ready.

qa.q: How might Kamal feel on reading the email?
qa.a: Kamal may feel a little embarrassed or defensive at first, but the calm tone and the clear request may make it easier to agree.

grounding: A person waiting on a late input rebuilds work overnight and explains the effect in a calm message.

subtype: Team hit by a late finisher [Receiver]
passage: At the cooperative bank in Hosur, Usha had to submit the month's loan report to the district office by Friday morning. She needed one set of figures from Shreya at the branch in the next village. Shreya promised them on Tuesday. On Wednesday the bus was cancelled and Shreya's line was busy. On Thursday afternoon the figures finally arrived by email, with two columns missing. Usha stayed back after closing. She called Shreya twice, filled in the gaps, checked the totals, and sent the report at eleven at night. Walking home in the dark, she felt tired and quietly resentful. The report was on time. Only she knew what it had cost.

qa.q: By when did Usha have to submit the loan report?
qa.a: By Friday morning.

qa.q: What was Usha feeling walking home in the dark?
qa.a: She felt tired and quietly resentful, knowing the report was on time only because she stayed late.

qa.q: What could Shreya do next time a promised date is slipping?
qa.a: Tell Usha on Wednesday that the figures would be late, so the work could be planned rather than squeezed into one night.

qa.q: How might Shreya see the report going in on time?
qa.a: Shreya might think the delay caused no harm, not seeing that Usha stayed until eleven to make up for it.

grounding: Shows a colleague who, waiting on someone else's late figures, has to stay late to meet her own deadline.

subtype: Team hit by a late finisher [Receiver]
passage: Emeka ran the product launch at a small software firm in Lagos. The website copy was ready, the ads were booked, and the launch was Monday. All he needed was the final app screenshots from Tomas, the designer. Tomas said Wednesday. Then Thursday. On Friday night the screenshots arrived, in the wrong size. Emeka spent Saturday resizing images, rewriting captions to match the new screens and calling the ad agency to push their deadline by a day. His sister's birthday lunch came and went without him. On Monday, the launch went live on time. Tomas sent a cheerful "Great launch!" message. Emeka stared at it for a long moment before replying.

qa.q: On what day was the launch?
qa.a: The launch was Monday.

qa.q: What does Emeka staring at Tomas's message suggest?
qa.a: It suggests he felt hurt and resentful, having given up his weekend and his sister's birthday lunch to cover the delay.

qa.q: What would you advise Tomas for the next launch?
qa.a: Warn Emeka as soon as the screenshots are slipping and check the required size, so the cost doesn't land silently on someone else.

qa.q: How does Tomas seem to see the launch?
qa.a: Tomas seems to see only the successful result and is unaware of Emeka's lost Saturday.

grounding: Shows a worker waiting on a colleague's late designs who has to compress his own work and give up his weekend.

subtype: Team hit by a late finisher [Receiver]
passage: The class six report cards had to reach the principal by Friday morning. In the school staffroom, Charu, the class teacher, had every subject's marks in her spreadsheet except science. Vikas had promised them on Tuesday. On Wednesday he said, "Tonight, pakka." On Thursday at 4:15 a message arrived: "Sorry, sorry, sending now." Charu stayed on as the cleaners switched off the corridor lights. She entered thirty-eight science scores, redid the averages, found that the rank list had shifted, and rewrote four remarks she had already printed. At 8:10 she texted her sister: "Can't make dinner. Save me some." Walking to the bus stop, her shoulders ached. Vikas would sleep fine tonight, she thought, and felt mean for thinking it, and then just tired.

qa.q: How many science scores did Charu enter on Thursday evening?
qa.a: She entered thirty-eight science scores.

qa.q: What was Charu feeling on the walk to the bus stop?
qa.a: She felt resentful that Vikas would sleep fine, then guilty for the thought, and above all exhausted after the long evening.

qa.q: What could Vikas have done on Tuesday that would have helped Charu?
qa.a: He could have told her on Tuesday that the marks were running late and given a real date, so she could plan her evening instead of losing it at the last minute.

qa.q: How might Vikas see the delay differently from Charu?
qa.a: Vikas may see it as a small slip covered by an apology, without seeing the four hours, the redone rank list and the missed dinner it cost her.

grounding: Shows a colleague who has to squeeze her own work and stay late because someone else's input arrived after the promised date.
